In this NYSE Live interview, Mark Miller, CEO and President of Universal Health Services (UHS), discusses the company's acquisition of Talkspace and its broader strategy for expanding behavioral healthcare services across inpatient, outpatient, and digital care settings.

Miller explains that UHS has historically been known for its inpatient behavioral health services while steadily building outpatient capabilities over the past several years. He describes the Talkspace acquisition as an important step in creating a more comprehensive behavioral healthcare platform capable of serving patients throughout different stages of treatment and recovery.

A major focus of the discussion is the concept of a full continuum of care. Miller explains how patients often require different levels of support over time and discusses the benefits of providing access to multiple treatment options within a connected healthcare system. These services may include inpatient care, outpatient programs, virtual therapy, and other behavioral health resources designed to support patient needs across various stages of care.

The conversation also highlights Talkspace's technology platform and digital healthcare capabilities. Miller discusses the company's expertise in virtual behavioral health services and explains how its technology infrastructure may create new opportunities for innovation and patient engagement within the broader UHS organization.

The interview further explores the role of artificial intelligence in behavioral healthcare. Miller discusses AI-powered tools developed within Talkspace's platform and shares his perspective on the importance of building healthcare-focused technologies designed specifically to support clinicians and patients in behavioral health settings.

Additional topics include capital allocation, healthcare technology investment, demand trends within behavioral health services, workforce considerations, and the company's long-term growth objectives. Miller explains how UHS continues to evaluate opportunities to expand access to care while maintaining a focus on quality, innovation, and patient outcomes.

Throughout the discussion, Miller provides insight into the evolving behavioral healthcare landscape and the growing intersection of healthcare delivery, digital services, and emerging technologies.
